<!-- kube-agents-bot:intro -->
Hello, I'm [**kube-agents-bot**](https://github.com/gke-labs/kube-agents-bot) 👋 I read
pull requests here and flag what looks wrong. I've started on this one — I'll post my
findings in a few minutes, or tell you I found none.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/review` | The strict read of the current commit: what I'm certain of, plus a high-severity finding just under that bar, marked as such. |
| `/review all` | The same read, kept wider — findings I checked and believe are real as well as the ones I'm certain of. This is what my first review of a pull request does. |
| `/review fresh` | Reads the commit again from scratch. Without it, a command on a commit I have already read re-cuts that read at the bar you asked for instead of reading again — same findings, other bar, no cost — and says so. |

Comment any of them on a line of its own. Repository owners, members and collaborators only.

Worth knowing:

- I review automatically when a pull request is **opened, reopened, or marked ready for
  review**. Pushing more commits does _not_ start a new review — comment `/review` when
  you want another look, or `/review all` for one as wide as the first. The one
  exception: if I said the branch doesn't merge, I'll start on my own after your next push.
- **I always say when I'm done**, even when I found nothing — so a review that finishes
  clean gets a short "no findings" note rather than silence, saying how I read the change
  and how many possible issues I checked on the way. The 👀 means I've started; a comment
  from me means I've finished. If you get 👀 and nothing follows, I broke.
- I only comment. I never push code, never merge, and I am not a required approval.
- Low-severity items I confirm — a literal that could be named, a sentence a change made
  stale — are folded into a collapsed list in my summary, not posted as findings, and
  don't count against the review. Whether to act on them is your call; nothing waits on
  them.
- I judge a change against the code, against any principles this repository has
  written down and pointed me at, and with the review method it has nominated, if it
  has one. Whether a feature or a design should exist at all is
  a human's call — a review from me saying nothing about that is not an endorsement.
- Label a pull request `agent:ignore` and I will leave it alone entirely, `/review`
  included.
- I can be wrong. Check anything I say before acting on it.

Held for one decision, described in Risk & Rollout: hack/ci-deploy.sh declares the bridge sidecar after the first provision Job has created TASKS at the 64 floor, so with this change the mode-next lane's second provision Job re-renders a wider budget (66 at 4 workers, 74 at 6) and the #2042 gate refuses it against the live 64-wide stream, leaving a Failed Job and a Degraded CR on every run while the eval still proceeds. The options are (a) declare the sidecar before the first provision, (b) set tuning.maxSessions on the eval CR to what fits 64, or (c) gate the second Job so the lane reds. Unhold once one is picked; (b) or (c) can be a follow-up commit on this branch.

<!-- coverage-report -->
## 📊 Coverage

**This PR's changed lines: no measurable lines changed 🟢** · Repository (Python): 80.5%

Report-only · nothing here blocks this pull request yet.

Decision on the hold: options (b) and (c) together. (b) hack/ci-deploy.sh sets `spec.tuning.maxSessions` on the eval CR to a value whose budget fits the 64-wide TASKS the first provision creates, before that first provision, so the sidecar patch never re-renders past the floor. (c) after the sidecar patch, the lane waits for the re-run provision Job and fails the step on `Degraded/A2AProvisionFailed` instead of proceeding over it, so a future budget move reds the lane rather than leaving a Failed Job behind. Note for (b): with #2010's look-ahead row the reserve is 6 per worker plus 20, so at 4 workers the largest maxSessions that fits 64 is 6 and at 6 workers it is 2; the eval spawns no session pods, so the value only has to be at least 1, and it should be derived or pinned against the Go constants rather than typed as a literal that drifts. The hold lifts when both are on the branch.

Both halves of the hold decision are on the branch: (b) `c04ee9f9` sizes `spec.harness.tuning.maxSessions` in the mode-next patch itself, from four script constants cross-pinned to the operator's (`TestCiDeploySizesMaxSessionsToTheTasksFloor`, `tests/test_ci_deploy_mode_next.py`), and (c) `b18c48fe` makes the lane wait for the re-run provision Job after the sidecar patch and red on a Failed Job or a `Degraded`/`A2AProvisionFailed` CR. The six ordering threads are resolved against them; Risk & Rollout is rewritten. The branch is also rebased over #2070 and carries #2010's look-ahead row (`e129fc62`), so the reserve is 20 + 6 per worker and the numbers in the description follow.

Two things before the hold comes off: the lane's own presubmit run on this head (`pull-kube-agents-smoke-test-next`) is the live check of (b)+(c), so I am waiting for it to go green rather than lifting on the unit tests alone; and the nightly, if it runs the next lane at 8 workers, now reds by design (the clamp gives `maxSessions=1` and the budget is still 71 on a 64-wide stream), which is what (c) asks for but is worth knowing before it fires. The two `ci(eval)` commits are new code past the five bot rounds; a `/review` on them is your call.

/hold cancel

The mode-next presubmit lane is green on `b18c48fe` (run 2105332433426583552, GREEN verdict, 6944 s), and both halves of the decision ran in it: the mode patch set `spec.harness.tuning.maxSessions=6 so the 64-wide TASKS holds the 4-worker bridge's budget (6*3 + 20 + 6*4 <= 64)`; after the sidecar patch the lane waited for the re-run provision Job `92d21508`, which completed 222-233 s after the patch, and the not-degraded gate read the CR at `Provisioning`, not `Degraded`; the rollout finished in 297 s and the eval ran. For comparison, the previous run of this lane on `4888c70c`, before (b)+(c), had the CR at `Degraded/A2AProvisionFailed` throughout and four cases failing the no-github-writes safeguard; on this run every one of those cases passed and the only PRs left on the infra repo are the pdb-remediation case's own. One run each, so that is a correlation to keep an eye on, not a finding. Lifting the hold per the decision; the required smoke is green too.

[APPROVALNOTIFIER] This PR is **APPROVED** This pull-request has been approved by: *bnaylor*, *jayantid* The full list of commands accepted by this bot can be found [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=gke-labs%2Fkube-agents). The pull request process is described [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/owners.md#the-code-review-process)
Needs approval from an approver in each of these files: - ~~[OWNERS](https://github.com/gke-labs/kube-agents/blob/main/OWNERS)~~ [bnaylor,jayantid] Approvers can indicate their approval by writing `/approve` in a comment Approvers can cancel approval by writing `/approve cancel` in a comment

commits.messageBody:
…'s BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY

The TASKS consumer budget's replay term counted the bridge's running
conversations at the bridge's compiled-in default of 2 workers, whatever
the CR declared. An install whose bridge sidecar sets BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY=6
rendered the same 64-wide stream and heard the same 28-consumer reserve in
the provision refusal as one at 2, while its bridge ran three times the
conversations the asks row was sized for.

The render now reads BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY off spec.deployment.sidecars the
way the bridge reads it off its environment: the sum over every sidecar
whose env sets it as a literal; the bridge's default for an empty,
non-integer, non-positive or valueFrom value, which is what the bridge
itself runs with; the default when no sidecar sets it. The reserve is that
table evaluated at the CR's worker count (28 at 2, 36 at 4, 44 at 6), the
budget and the rendered max_consumers move with it, and the provision
script's refusal quotes the reserve it used and the worker count behind it.

The default-install constants stay as the table, and
TestReservedConsumersIsTheSumOfItsTerms holds the function at the default
equal to the literal, so gke-labs#2010's look-ahead row lands in both
spellings or fails there.

Part of gke-labs#2043 (item 2). Item 1, the bridge's handling of a refused
replay, is owned elsewhere.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): size the TASKS consumer budget from the bridge sidecar…

commits.messageBody:
…e refusal names both inputs and the third way out

The bridge count a2aBridgeConcurrency summed off spec.deployment.sidecars
had no upper bound, because the bridge has none: envInt takes any integer
strconv.Atoi returns and Config.defaults rewrites only a count below one.
BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY="1000000000" rendered --max-consumers=4000000050, and
"9223372036854775807" wrapped the replay term negative, took the reserve
to 16 - below the default install's 28 - and passed the gate on a stream
that was short. The count is now capped at a2aBridgeConcurrencyMax =
1024, the bridge's own taskQueueCapacity and the ceiling hack/ci-deploy.sh
already puts on EVAL_TASK_PARALLELISM; the CRD bounds the other input,
maxSessions, at 10000 for the same wrap, and at both ceilings the budget
is 34116. A literal above the cap counts as the cap, not the default,
which would size a large install short; the sum over sidecars is capped
the same way; and the provision script's refusal and the status message
say when the count was capped. TestBridgeConcurrencyMaxMatchesTheBridgeQueue
reads the bridge's constant, and TestBridgeConcurrencyIsCappedBeforeTheArithmetic
holds a literal above the cap, MaxInt64 and two sidecars past the cap
to the cap and the reserve above the default's; removing the clamp
fails both and the capped rows of
TestBridgeConcurrencyReadsTheSidecarLikeTheBridgeDoes.

The failed-Job status message and the rendered refusal named maxSessions
alone and offered two remedies, so the install gke-labs#2043 describes -
a bus provisioned at 64 with budget 58, then a sidecar declared at 4 -
read "maxSessions=10 needs (66)" although maxSessions=10 fit before the
sidecar. Where the CR declares more workers than the bridge's default,
both surfaces now attribute the need to maxSessions and the worker count
and offer the third lever, fewer workers (or no BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY),
which re-renders the Job the way a maxSessions edit does; the script
computes the worker count that fits beside the CR's maxSessions from the
live stream the way it computes the maxSessions that fits, and says when
none does. At the default the two surfaces read as they did.
TestProvisionRefusalOffersFewerBridgeWorkers executes the script on that
install and on the default one, TestProvisionFailureStatusNamesBothInputs
holds the status message in both shapes and through the reconcile, and
TestProvisionRefusalNamesTheReserveItSizedFor gains the case where the
lever does not reach; disabling either surface's bridge-aware branch
fails them.

Part of gke-labs#2043 (item 2).

commits.messageBody:
…he kubelet expands it

The kubelet expands $(NAME) references in a container's env[].value against
the entries declared before it in the same container, in declaration order,
before the process starts. A sidecar declared as EVAL_PARALLELISM=6,
BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY=$(EVAL_PARALLELISM) therefore runs six bridge workers,
and a render that ran strconv.Atoi on the literal counted the default of 2,
budgeted 58, created TASKS at 64 and passed the gate: the under-sizing this
PR exists to remove, with no refusal to say so.

a2aBridgeConcurrencyValue now walks the sidecar's env the way the kubelet's
makeEnvironmentVariables does: each literal entry is expanded against what
came before it and remembered under its name, so a reference through an
earlier reference resolves in declaration order; a valueFrom entry is
remembered as unknowable, so a reference to it, or to a literal a later
valueFrom shadows, is left as written, fails Atoi and takes the default; the
last entry of the name counts. expandEnvReferences follows expansion.Expand
(k8s.io/kubernetes/third_party/forked/golang/expansion, not a dependency
here): $(NAME) becomes the known value or is left as written, $$ is one $,
and a $ followed by anything else, an unclosed $( included, is literal.
Nothing this render emits changes: the sidecar is still copied verbatim,
and only BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY is read through the expansion.

The reserve comment, a2aBridgeConcurrencyOf's doc, the provision script's
parenthetical and spec-nats-deployment.md no longer say a non-integer
literal is what the bridge runs with; they say what is readable, a literal
or a $(NAME) reference to an earlier literal in the same sidecar, and that
a valueFrom or a reference to one is the default.

Pinned in TestBridgeConcurrencyReadsTheSidecarLikeTheBridgeDoes (eleven new
rows: the reference, the chain, the self-reference, textual expansion, a
later entry, a valueFrom, a shadowed literal, an undeclared name, $$, an
unclosed $(, and a reference above the cap) and in
TestTasksBudgetReadsTheBridgeSidecarConcurrency (three rows through the
budget, the render and the script). TestProvisionRefusalNamesTheReserveItSizedFor
now also asserts the executed script prints the literal $(NAME), which the
echo's double quotes would otherwise run as a command substitution.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): the budget reads a $(VAR) BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY the way t…

commits.messageBody:
… an entry took the default

a2aProvisionRefusalStatus attributed the worker count to the CR ("the 8
bridge workers the CR declares") when the count is a2aBridgeWorkers' sum
and an entry it could not read as a count - a valueFrom, a reference to
one, a value the bridge would not take - counted as the bridge's default
of 2. A CR with one sidecar at 6 and one whose BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY is a
configMapKeyRef declares 6 and a reference, not 8. The rendered script's
parenthetical already stated the per-entry rule; the status message, the
surface the Ready row points at, did not.

a2aBridgeConcurrencyOf and a2aBridgeWorkers report a third value,
defaulted, set only when an entry that sets the key took the default in
its place (never when no sidecar sets it, or the CR wrote 2 out). The
numbers do not change. Where it is set the message says "the N bridge
workers the render reads from spec.deployment.sidecars (BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY;
an entry it cannot read as a count, a valueFrom or a reference to one
among them, counts as the bridge's default of 2)", and the capped sentence
that follows opens "That count is more than 1024" instead of "The CR
declares more than 1024". Where every entry was a count the sentence is
unchanged. At the default there is no worker sentence, so no clause.

TestProvisionFailureStatusNamesBothInputs pins both shapes, the lone
$(NAME)-to-a-valueFrom case at the default, and the capped-over-a-read
case; TestBridgeConcurrencyReadsTheSidecarLikeTheBridgeDoes pins the flag
per row. Forcing defaulted false fails the two new status cases and 13
rows of the terms test.

Docs: the Ready row and spec-nats-deployment.md say the refusal states
when an entry took the default. Separately, the Ready row still said
"one of the two remedies" from before this branch's round-1 fix made it
three ways out; it now reads "one of those ways out - the two, or the
three where the fewer-workers lever is offered".
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): the refusal status says what the render read, and when…

commits.messageBody:
…read, and the status names a 1-worker reserve

a2aBridgeWorkers reported defaulted, and a2aProvisionScript threw it away:
the per-entry rule was printed only inside the refusal branch, so a CR
whose only BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY is a valueFrom resolved to 2, budgeted 58,
passed a 64-wide stream and ran its real worker count on a stream sized
for two with nothing in any log to say so - the under-sizing gke-labs#2043
names, reached with no refusal. A key delivered through the sidecar's
envFrom was the same silence from further off: a2aBridgeConcurrencyValue
walks env, so set was false and the sidecar looked like no bridge. The
script now prints a NOTE on every run, exit 0 included, in the shape of
the max_msgs_per_subject drift report - before the gate, exiting nothing -
when an entry took the default in place of a count the render could not
read (what it counted, that the bridge may run more, and to set a literal
or a $(NAME) reference to an earlier literal in the same entry), and,
through the new a2aBridgeEnvFromUnread, when a sidecar carries envFrom and
sets no BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY in env (a key delivered that way is not read,
and a literal in env overrides it). No number moves: envFrom is not a
declared bridge. TestProvisionSaysWhenABridgeCountWasNotRead executes the
script on all five shapes - a valueFrom alone, an envFrom alone, a literal
beside envFrom, a literal alone, no sidecar - and pins exit 0, budget 58,
which NOTE prints and which does not; dropping the emission fails the
first two.

a2aProvisionRefusalStatus gated the worker sentence on workers > default,
so a CR at BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY=1 - reserve 24, not 28 - read
"maxSessions=20 needs (84)" with no mention of the input that shaped the
number, while the script's note said "sized for 1 bridge workers". The
attribution now goes out whenever the declared count moved the reserve
(workers != default); the fewer-workers lever, the three-ways-out wording
and the worker-count-that-fits stay above the default, where a lower count
exists, and at one worker the clause says "with no lower count left to
declare". Both surfaces say "1 bridge worker". The script's workers_fit
lever was already above-default only and is unchanged.
TestProvisionFailureStatusNamesBothInputs gains the 1-worker/20-sessions
row and keeps the default-2 row with no worker sentence; reverting the
gate fails the new row.

Drift from this branch's own earlier rounds, folded in:
- buildA2AProvisionJob's comment said the daily re-create re-checks against a recreated stream or a lowered maxSessions; a lowered worker count is a third.
- reconcileA2A's comment above the refusal branch described a two-way remedy; it names the worker-count lever, offered only above the default.
- The maxSessions CRD field description said the refusal names "the two ways out"; it now says two, or three for a CR declaring more workers than the default. CRD regenerated (config/crd/bases, charts/kube-agents/crds via chart-sync); no other generated file moved.
- spec-nats-deployment.md and the site Ready row credited the script's refusal with the "when an entry took the default" sentence the status message carries; each sentence is now attributed to the surface that carries it, and the NOTE is named as the success-path surface.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): the provision script says when a bridge count was not …

commits.messageBody:
…unreadable entries summed to the default

a2aProvisionRefusalStatus gated the "what the render read" clause on
workers != default, so a CR whose only BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY entry was a
valueFrom, a reference to one or to a later entry, a non-integer or a 0
resolved to the default with defaulted set and was refused as
"maxSessions=N needs (B)" with no mention of the bridge, while the
sidecar may run more workers off its ConfigMap than the budget sized
for. The design doc, the site's Ready row and the rule block above the
constants all say the clause fires whenever an entry took the default.
The gate now also opens on defaulted; at the default the reserve is
stated once, as the default's, and the ways out stay two. A literal 2
on the CR, or no entry, still has no worker sentence; every other shape
is byte-identical. The test row that pinned the old behaviour now
expects the clause, and fails with the gate reverted.

The comment over TestTasksBudgetReadsTheBridgeSidecarConcurrency said
it runs against a tree without the resolver; it no longer compiles on
one. It now says what is true: such a tree produces 58, 64 and 28 on
every shape, and the rows that declare a count expect otherwise.

The rendered script's exit-2 comment said both numbers are fixed until
maxSessions comes down or the stream is recreated; it now names the
budget's two inputs and the fewer-workers lever where the CR declared
more than the default.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): the refusal status states the read rule even when the …

commits.messageBody:
… and every number follows

gke-labs#2010 landed the bridge's pre-spawn look-ahead and put
a2aTasksReplayBridgeLookAhead = a2aBridgeDefaultConcurrency back in the
a2aTasksReplayConsumers sum, which this branch's own comment said was the
day the same row goes inside a2aTasksReplayConsumersFor as one slot per
worker. It does now: a2aTasksReplayLookAhead = 1 per worker sits beside
a2aTasksReplayAsk, a2aTasksReplayBridgeLookAhead is that at the default,
and TestReservedConsumersIsTheSumOfItsTerms holds the two spellings equal
at a2aBridgeDefaultConcurrency again.

The reserve, re-derived from the terms:

    reserve(w) = 16 + a2aTasksReplayTailFactor * (1 + 1 + 2w + w)
               = 20 + 6w

    | workers | reserve | budget at maxSessions=10 | first refused on a 64-wide TASKS |
    | ------: | ------: | -----------------------: | -------------------------------: |
    |       1 |      26 |                       56 |                     maxSessions 13 |
    |       2 |      32 |            62, renders 64 |                     maxSessions 11 |
    |       4 |      44 |                       74 |                      maxSessions 7 |
    |       6 |      56 |                       86 |                      maxSessions 3 |
    |    1024 |    6164 |                     6194 |                                  - |

The default is 32, as main has it; each worker past the default adds 6
(two asks and one look-ahead, each with its tail), not 4. The provision
script's workers_fit is (live - maxSessions*3 - 20) / 6, one worker beside
one session needs 29, and the cap arithmetic is 10000*3 + 20 + 6*1024 =
36164. Every number the constants-block comment, the provision script,
the status message and the two budget test files state moved with it;
main's look-ahead table and prose stay as gke-labs#2010 wrote them, with
the per-worker sentences added beside them.

The CRD description and the docs this branch touches quote no reserve
number, so nothing there moves.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(operator): the per-worker reserve carries #2010's look-ahead row,…

commits.messageBody:
…e first provision (#2077 (b))

The mode-next lane patches the mode and the bridge sidecar separately (a
bridge that starts before NATS resolves crash-loops the agent pod), so
the first provision Job creates TASKS for a CR with no sidecar -- at the
64 floor, since 10*3 + 32 = 62 -- and the sidecar patch re-renders the
Job with BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY=EVAL_TASK_PARALLELISM in the reserve. At the
presubmit's 4 workers that budget is 74, the second run refuses against
the stream the first created, and the CR parks Degraded over a working
bus while the lane goes green. The tech lead's decision on the hold
(2026-09-30): size the first provision for the sidecar.

The mode patch now also sets spec.harness.tuning.maxSessions, in the
same merge so the first render sees both. Section 2b sizes it at second
zero, from the concurrency the guard there admitted:

    maxSessions = floor((A2A_TASKS_FLOOR - A2A_RESERVE_FIXED
                         - A2A_RESERVE_PER_WORKER * workers)
                        / A2A_SESSION_CONSUMERS), clamped to >= 1

with A2A_TASKS_FLOOR=64, A2A_SESSION_CONSUMERS=3, A2A_RESERVE_FIXED=20
and A2A_RESERVE_PER_WORKER=6, the reserve table with #2010's look-ahead
row. That is 6 at 4 workers (18 + 44 = 62), 2 at 6 (6 + 56 = 62), and
the clamp's 1 at 8 or more, where the floor cannot hold the reserve
(3 + 68 = 71) and the second Job refuses; the eval spawns no session
pods, so the value only has to be API-legal. The lane's log states the
arithmetic beside the value, for a reader of the artifact who finds a
non-default maxSessions on the eval CR.

The four numbers are copied, not typed as one literal: the operator's
are Go constants a shell script cannot evaluate. They are pinned on both
sides. TestCiDeploySizesMaxSessionsToTheTasksFloor reads the script,
holds each to a2aTasksMaxConsumersFloor, a2aSessionConsumersPerSession,
a2aTasksReservedConsumersFor(0) and the table's slope, holds the table
linear at every count the lane can run, decodes MODE_NEXT_PATCH_FORMAT
into the PlatformAgent type with unknown fields refused (the path is the
CRD's), and holds the promise itself: at 4 and 6 workers the first
render creates TASKS at the floor and the second budget fits it; at 8
it does not. tests/test_ci_deploy_mode_next.py pins the same four to
the Go literals, runs section 2b's arithmetic at 1..1024 workers, and
pins the log line, the patch's rendering, the patch and the first Job
wait in that order, with no other patch ahead of it. Either pin fails
with any one of the four moved on either side (checked by mutating the
script's A2A_RESERVE_FIXED and A2A_TASKS_FLOOR).

Nothing else in the lane or in bench/ assumes the default maxSessions.
The design doc's executor paragraph, which said sizing the first
provision was owed, now says how it is sized.
commits.messageHeadline: ci(eval): size the eval CR's maxSessions to the TASKS floor before th…

commits.messageBody:
…eds on A2AProvisionFailed (#2077 (c))

The sidecar's BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY is an input to the TASKS consumer
budget, so the sidecar patch re-renders the provision Job, and its
second run measures the new budget against the stream the first run
created. The lane did not wait for that run or read the CR after it: a
refusal parked the CR Degraded over a working bus while the step went
on to a green bridge line, which is how the hold on this PR was found.
The other half of the tech lead's decision (2026-09-30): wait for the
re-run and fail the step on it, so a future budget move reds the lane
rather than leaving a Failed Job behind.

The inline Job wait is now wait_provision_job. Its first call is the
old gate, name-aware: the read lists each provision Job with its True
conditions, a Complete on any counted Job passes, a Failed with no
Complete elsewhere fails, and the Job that passed is kept as
FIRST_PROVISION_JOB. After the sidecar patch and the generation wait
it is called again with that name and the CR generation the patch
produced, and does not count the superseded Job: it is Complete, and
it stays listed until the operator's next pass sweeps it, which is
after that pass has rolled the agent Deployment (reconcileA2A runs
after reconcileWorkload), so the read right after the generation moves
can still show only the old run. A render the patch did not change
keeps the old Job -- same digest, same name -- and there is nothing to
wait for; that case is told from "not created yet" by the CR's
status.observedGeneration reaching the patched generation, written at
the end of the pass that would have created a new one. Jobs are not
watched by the operator, so a Failed re-run reaches the CR's Ready
condition on the requeue that reads it; the failure waits up to
MODE_NEXT_STATUS_ATTEMPTS polls for that condition, prints it beside
the Job's describe and pod log, and exits 1. After a Complete re-run,
gate_cr_not_degraded reads the CR once and exits 1 on phase Degraded or
a Ready reason of A2AProvisionFailed, printing the condition either
way. Both sit between the sidecar generation wait and the agent rollout
gate; the later gates keep their order.

tests/test_ci_deploy_mode_next.py lifts the functions whole and runs
them against a kubectl stub: the old gate's four terminal cases and its
timing bounds, a re-run Complete beside the old Job, an old Complete
that must not count for a running re-run, an unchanged render observed
versus not yet observed, a Failed re-run carrying the operator's
refusal with the bounded status wait, the Degraded gate's five phase
and reason combinations, and the gate order with the two new calls in
it. The status words are pinned to the controller source, as is the
reconcile ordering the wait relies on and the absence of a Job watch.

With (b) on the branch the re-run completes at the presubmit's 4
workers and at 6; at 8 or more the floor cannot hold the reserve, and
this is the guard that makes that a red lane with the refusal in the
log rather than a green one with a Failed Job behind it. The design doc
now says the lane waits for the re-run and reds on a refusal.
commits.messageHeadline: ci(eval): the mode-next lane waits for the re-run provision Job and r…

commits.messageBody:
…for the reserve

hermes-bridge.md still said the operator renders the bridge with no operator
code and leaves BRIDGE_CONCURRENCY unset, so a wider bridge could outgrow the
reserve. Since this change the render reads the sidecar's entry and sizes the
TASKS consumer reserve from it, and a value the stream's floor cannot hold is
